My Interests & My Reasons for the Interest

          
A personal reflection on the engineering problems I care about and why I build practical spatial and AI systems in Nepal.

        

      


      

        

          My Interests
          
        

        
I love building software that connects complex spatial data with everyday life on the ground. Over the past five years working as a Geomatics Engineer and software developer in Nepal, my curiosity has grown from traditional land surveying and mapping into full-stack web engineering, deep learning computer vision for aerial imagery and legal AI retrieval systems. Whether I am designing a fast 3D map engine that renders thousands of buildings smoothly in a browser, training neural networks to trace rooftops from drone orthophotos or indexing the Constitution of Nepal for instant semantic search, I enjoy turning heavy technical challenges into simple and responsive tools that anyone can use.

      


      

        

          My Reasons for the Interest
          
        

        
Working across municipalities and engineering projects in Nepal showed me firsthand how much local planners, engineers and communities rely on clear and accessible digital infrastructure. When spatial records, road network maps and public legal documents are locked inside slow desktop software or scattered across disconnected files, everyday planning and public decision-making become much harder than they need to be. That experience is the main reason I care so deeply about bringing together geospatial engineering, practical machine learning and transparent web systems. I want the tools I build to bridge the gap between raw field data and real human needs so people can plan infrastructure, explore public laws and make informed decisions with confidence.
